evidence: The engine's tree-sitter-typescript grammar (0.23.2 with Rerail's patches, native/grammars) does not parse an index signature without a type annotation (`type Foo = { [key: string] };`): on this file the engine reports source-partial ("file has syntax errors") and the rule misses the finding upstream reports on the type alias. typescript-eslint 8.70.1 parses it, and TypeScript 6.0.3's parser reads it with no parse diagnostics; only TypeScript's checker rejects it (TS1021, an index signature must have a type annotation). The file is one of consistent-indexed-object-style's upstream tests; Rerail cannot decide it until the grammar reads the construct.
